reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that scientific progress hinges on the interplay between public knowledge and hidden potential. The informational existence of phenomena like atomic reactions is a foundational datum, yet the true secret lies in the possibility of constructing such systems—this is the \( \mathcal{I}_{\text{secret}} \). When scientists know a problem has an answer, their attitude shifts dramatically, implying a phase transition in \( \mathcal{A}(t) \). The emergence of collaborative knowledge pools, enabled by global scientific networks, allows for unprecedented synthesis of individual \( \mathcal{K}_i \). These primitives form a dual structure: \( \mathcal{I}_{\text{exist}} \) and \( \mathcal{I}_{\text{secret}} \) define the informational landscape, while \( \mathcal{A}(t) \) and \( \mathcal{K}_{\text{pool}} \) govern the dynamics of belief and cooperation. Failure modes include \( \mathcal{I}_{\text{secret}} \to 0 \) leading to stagnation, and \( \mathcal{A}(t) \to \text{randomness} \) due to lack of structured problem framing.
